subject: Selecting anchor items when using DIF

messages.author: 9403604069d4685f
messages.subject: Selecting anchor items when using DIF
parts:
Dear Phil,

When using the DIF function, it is suggested that we should use anchor items and free the hyperparameters.
However, I'm not sure what would be the best way to pick the anchor items and how many of them should there be in relation to test length.
Do you perhaps have any guidelines for this or are there some papers that you would recommend on this topic?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Selecting anchor items when using DIF
parts:
This is a good question, and one worth investigating via research. In general, anchors must be selected based on a priori invariant items for them to work, where the theoretical minimum number of parameters to constrain is at least 1 slope and one intercept (though clearly that's not the most optimal idea), and the stability of the IRT model also makes a difference. More anchors the better, but of course this requires stronger prior knowledge as well. There have been algorithmic approaches to try and solve this problem based on alternative selection criteria (e.g., see the work by Carol Woods), but I'm not completely sure how much I trust these algorithms just yet without testing them myself. 

Phil
